F1: Adding an existing member violates the unique index, and earlier additions remain committed when the request fails.
F2: Removal bypasses the cleanup that clears primary_group_id, leaving removed members associated with the group on posts.
F3: Exact multiples produce an extra page, allowing navigation to an empty member list.
F4: Removing the final member on the last page leaves the offset beyond the remaining records without correction.
F5: The public members page fetches only 50 members and provides no pagination or load-more control.
F6: Negative limits and offsets reach PostgreSQL unchecked and cause request failures.
F7: Add and remove requests have no rejection handler to display failures to the admin.
F8: Ignoring alias_level during creation is a pre-existing defect, not behavior introduced by this change.
